title: Spend Your Time Wisely
coreMove: Choose the compounding activity by naming the best alternative it displaces and the present-bias reward that will try to steal the slot.
sourcePressure: The source combines compound interest, opportunity cost, and present bias: small repeated gains stack, but every choice excludes another, and near-term rewards sabotage long-term progress.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: Treating time wisdom as doing more tasks faster rather than protecting the few repeated choices that can compound.

sourceAnchors.name: compound interest
sourceAnchors.detail: the source explains compounding as gains that accelerate because prior gains are added back into the base
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: The first repeats look small because the base is still small; the power arrives when yesterday’s gain joins today’s work.

sourceAnchors.name: fitness goals and procrastination
sourceAnchors.detail: the source uses procrastination and fitness goals as the concrete frame for present bias
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: Present bias rarely announces itself as sabotage; it arrives as one comfortable skip that steals from the body you wanted later.

hook: You can do anything but not everything
Time is your most valuable asset
tryThisNow: Block time for your most important goal
Set a timer for focused work

exampleSpecs.domain: Emily, a public defender protecting ninety minutes each morning for case review before court calls begin
exampleSpecs.audience: professionals whose urgent requests crowd out compounding preparation
exampleSpecs.stakes: a missed detail could affect a plea negotiation
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Emily turns down a nonurgent committee invite by naming the specific case-review block it would displace
exampleSpecs.firstImage: the courthouse hallway smells like wet wool and burnt coffee

exampleSpecs.domain: Mathieu, a conservatory pianist choosing slow scales over another flashy recital piece
exampleSpecs.audience: learners tempted by visible short-term rewards
exampleSpecs.stakes: technical weakness will cap his auditions if he keeps chasing applause pieces
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Mathieu writes the audition skill that compounds from scales and crosses off the crowd-pleasing piece that would eat the same hour
exampleSpecs.firstImage: It took Mathieu four auditions to admit the fast piece was hiding the same weak left hand

exampleSpecs.domain: Sophie, a municipal gardener choosing soil improvement over another row of showy annuals
exampleSpecs.stakes: the park can look bright this month while growing weaker for next season
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Sophie puts the compost order beside the flower invoice and chooses the slower work because the soil base will carry future blooms
exampleSpecs.firstImage: rain beads on a pallet of compost bags beside a tray of red annuals

exampleSpecs.domain: Lars, a freelance translator refusing a low-margin rush job to protect a certification-study evening
exampleSpecs.audience: independent workers facing opportunity cost in cash terms
exampleSpecs.stakes: tonight’s fee would delay the credential that raises future rates
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Lars calculates the rush fee against the exam slot it would consume and declines the job with a specific alternative date
exampleSpecs.firstImage: At 6:12 p.m., Lars reads the rush-job email with his exam book already open

exampleSpecs.domain: Catarina, a medical resident choosing sleep before a surgical rotation instead of one more hour of review videos
exampleSpecs.audience: high-achievers who confuse present effort with future payoff
exampleSpecs.stakes: fatigue could erase the benefit of extra study
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Catarina says what the extra hour would cost tomorrow, closes the laptop, and preserves the compounding base of rested learning
exampleSpecs.firstImage: “What does this hour take from rounds tomorrow?”

exampleSpecs.domain: Chidi, a community radio producer choosing weekly archive cleanup over chasing a viral segment idea
exampleSpecs.audience: creative workers balancing maintenance and novelty
exampleSpecs.stakes: lost clips and messy rights notes will keep future episodes from shipping
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Chidi opens the missing-rights spreadsheet, sees the compounding drag, and schedules the cleanup before approving the viral idea
exampleSpecs.firstImage: You do not hear archive debt until the guest tape is missing

tryThisNowSpec: Pick one invitation or task from the next two days and write the best thing it would displace; decline, defer, or protect the slot if the displaced thing compounds more.

exampleOpeningDiversity.rule: no more than 2 of the 6 examples may open with the pattern 'At HH:MM, <Name> <verb>s'
exampleOpeningDiversity.requiredOpenings: at least 4 distinct opening devices across the 6 examples, drawn from: timestamp+name+action, dialogue first line, sensory detail first, second-person direct address, retrospective, question-as-hook, environmental detail before any human
exampleOpeningDiversity.rationale: C8 catches Cartesian repetition of phrases but not the deeper template of 'timestamp + named protagonist + prop + decision' that makes 6 examples feel like 1 example with name swaps

skillTargets: identify the chapter-specific model in a fresh scenario for Spend Your Time Wisely
choose the visible action that performs the core move rather than naming the concept
explain the failure mode that appears when the model is used generically
evaluate tradeoffs and limits without sliding into certainty, cynicism, or manipulation

rhythmVariety.deepReadParagraphLengthMix: at least one paragraph 3 sentences or shorter, at least one paragraph 5+ sentences, at least one one-sentence punch line
rhythmVariety.fullReadInterludeRequirement: at least one paragraph that breaks the scene-then-rule rhythm: a question to the reader, a research aside, a direct second-person passage, or a brief historical reference
rhythmVariety.forbiddenRhythm: every paragraph following the pattern 'concrete anchor sentence -> abstract rule sentence -> elaboration sentence'
